# Pages: sites in TSX, TypeScript or EJS

Put a `.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.ejs` or `.md` file in a `pb_pages` folder next to `pb_data`, and your app serves it as a web
page. Each file is a route. Components `import` each other, a `.ts` file runs (a page's code beside it, or an endpoint), and
page code reads and writes your records directly. Every part of a page can `await`, and the app keeps serving other
requests while it waits. This is Pages, built into PocketOne.

esbuild is built into the `pocketone` binary, so TSX and TypeScript compile the first time a page is used: no Node, no
`npm install`, no bundler, no build step. It's on for every PocketOne app whenever a `pb_pages` folder exists. No folder,
no pages.

## A product page in TSX

The page is an `async` component: it awaits its record, then renders it with another component.

```tsx
// pb_pages/products/[id].tsx
import Price from './_private/Price'

export default async function Product({ ctx }: any) {
  const product = await ctx.app.findRecordById.async('products', ctx.params.id)
  return (
    <article>
      <h1>{product.getString('name')}</h1>
      <Price cents={product.getInt('price')} />
    </article>
  )
}
```

```tsx
// pb_pages/products/_private/Price.tsx
export default ({ cents }: { cents: number }) => <span class="price">${(cents / 100).toFixed(2)}</span>
```

`/products/<id>` now answers with `<article><h1>Mug</h1><span class="price">$12.50</span></article>`. Edit any of the
files and reload: the change shows up with no restart.

## await anywhere

`.async` twins of Go functions (`findRecordById.async`, `countRecords.async`, ...) do their work
outside the JS VM, so the app serves other requests while a page waits.

- **Components:** any component can be `async`. Sibling components run at the same time, so these two counts load in
  parallel:

  ```tsx
  async function Count({ collection }: { collection: string }) {
    const n = await $app.countRecords.async(collection)
    return <b>{n}</b>
  }

  export default () => <p><Count collection="orders" /> orders, <Count collection="users" /> users</p>
  ```

- **Loaders and handlers:** `load`, `get`, `post` and the rest in a page's `.ts` or an endpoint, and `+middleware`
  can be `async`.
- **EJS:** a tag can `await`: `<% const n = await ctx.app.countRecords.async('orders') %>`.
- **Sync stays free:** a page without `await` runs exactly as before.

[Loading data](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/loading-data#async-loading), [EJS](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ejs#await) and
[JSX and TSX](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/jsx#async-components) have the details.

JSX renders to plain HTML on the server. There's no virtual DOM and no client-side React, so pair it with htmx,
Datastar or plain `<script>` tags for interactivity. TypeScript types are stripped, not checked; run `tsc --noEmit` or
rely on your editor. [JSX and TSX](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/jsx) has the details.

## Prefer EJS? Hello world

1. Make a folder for your app with a page in it:

   ```bash
   mkdir -p myapp/pb_pages && cd myapp
   echo '<%= `Hello, world!` %>' > pb_pages/index.ejs
   ```

2. Create a superuser, then start the app:

   ```bash
   pocketone superuser upsert you@example.com <password> --dir ./pb_data
   pocketone serve --dir ./pb_data
   ```

3. Open http://127.0.0.1:8090. You see `Hello, world!`

Edit the file and reload the browser. Changes show up right away, with no restart.

To start from something bigger, `pocketone pages starters` lists the starter kits and
`pocketone pages create myapp --starter <kit>` makes a new app from one.

## What's covered

- **Files are routes:** `pb_pages/about.ejs` serves `/about`, and `pb_pages/blog/index.ejs` serves `/blog`.
- **Templates:** TSX, JSX, EJS and Markdown, mixed freely (an EJS page can sit in a TSX layout), with layouts,
  partials, middleware and JSON routes. A route's code is a `.ts` file (`about.ts` beside `about.ets`, or an endpoint like `feeds/rss.ts`); `.js` files are served to the browser.
- **Leftovers go on:** a URL no page matches goes on to `pb_public`, then to PocketBase. URLs under `/api/` and `/_/`
  always belong to PocketBase.
- **Errors:** in dev mode you get detailed error pages. Otherwise visitors see a plain error page and the details go to
  the log.
- **Not with `--jsvm goja`:** pages run in PocketOne's own JS engine, so they're off when you serve with PocketBase's.

To send your pages to a running app, see [Deploy and live sync](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/deploy).

## Change it

To serve pages from another folder, pass `--pagesDir` to `pocketone serve`, or set `server.pages_dir` in
`pocketone.yaml` ([pocketone.yaml reference](https://pocketone.dev/docs/config-reference)). Settings for the site itself, such as which
Pages plugins to load, go in `pb_pages/+config.js` ([+config.js](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/config)).

## How it works

- [Pages](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/extension) serves the `pb_pages` folder and adds the `pages create` and
  `pages starters` commands. Page code runs in your app's JS engine.
- [Pages](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages) is the home of its docs, guides and plugins.
